detail: MissingCore/Music is discarded as the react-native-android second application rather than retried further. The measurement is unambiguous and is a property of that application: seeding calls MediaStore's scan_file per fixture and scan_volume for the external volume through the content provider, then queries the audio volume back and confirms all four fixtures indexed before the application is launched, and with the media permission then granted the application's library still reports zero tracks for the full 300 second bound. Making that application ingest an already populated volume is not harness work. streetwriters/notesnook replaces it and is selected on evidence rather than on the recorded list: it is already qualified here as offline with a skippable signup, its release signingConfig uses the committed debug.keystore so it builds with no secret, and notesnook-unlink-notebook-10053 has a verified pair, affected 14f727d6 and fixed 7c3fdab6, whose diff is confined to apps/mobile/app/screens/link-notebooks/index.tsx and reads exactly as the issue describes: in single-select mode the fix diffs the initial selection against the current one and writes an explicit deselected state, so on the affected build a notebook the user removed stays linked to the note. Both revisions are bootstrapped, the workspace bootstrap completes, and the iOS pods resolve at both. Its Android build has not completed. It does not fail, it stalls, and the cause is the same one the WebDriverAgent bisection found: syspolicyd on this build host is wedged near a full core and processes Gradle spawns sleep in _dyld_start without executing an instruction, first the React Native autolinking node during the settings phase and then the editor bundle's vite. The identical commands run instantly from an interactive shell, so it is neither the binary nor the script. Two workarounds are committed to the record rather than hidden: the autolink config is generated once from a shell and fed to Gradle with autolinkLibrariesFromCommand(["/bin/cat", <file>]), which produces byte-identical autolinking without spawning node, and the build is driven by a bounded retry loop because Gradle's up-to-date checks make each attempt resume where the last stalled. That combination has carried the build from the settings phase through configuration and into compilation. No promotion is claimed and no run is recorded that was not performed.
